title: The integral closure of a domain in an algebraic extension of its fraction field is a normal domain with that field as fraction field
statement: Let $P$ be an integral domain with field of fractions $K$, let $L$ be a field extension of $K$ which is algebraic (every element of $L$ is a root of a nonzero polynomial in $K[T]$), and let $R=\{\alpha\in L:\alpha$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in $P\}$ be the integral closure of $P$ in $L$. Then $R$ is a subring of $L$ containing $P$ (so $R$ is an integral domain and $R$ is integral over $P$), $L$ is a field of fractions of $R$ (the inclusion $R\subseteq L$ extends to an isomorphism $\operatorname{Frac}(R)\xrightarrow{\sim}L$), and $R$ is integrally closed in $L$; hence $R$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring].

source.place: Lemma 00GO (label lemma-integral-closure-is-ring, line 7542: the integral closure is a subring); Lemma 0308 (lemma-integral-closure-transitive, line 7723: R is integrally closed in L); Lemma 034L (lemma-integral-closure-in-normal, line 7985); the fraction field statement is the clearing of denominators of an algebraic element (for alpha in L with a_n alpha^n + ... + a_0 = 0, a_i in P, a_n != 0, the element a_n alpha is integral over P)
